statement: The historical and adopted localizer axioms are different formulations. The literal Loc~(1) of XVI ms.~1 consists of isomorphisms, two-out-of-three, and the condition that $gf,fg\in W$ imply $f,g\in W$. Grothendieck calls the first two conditions \emph{saturation faible}, and all three \emph{saturation mod\'er\'ee}. Retract closure is added in Loc~(1 bis); strong saturation is Loc~(1 ter). The literal Loc~(3), XVI ms.~2, is absolute Theorem~A. Relative Theorem~A is Loc~(3 bis), ms.~3. In this paper, a fundamental localizer means the modern relative package specified in the conventions: weak saturation, the terminal-object axiom, and the assertion that a functor $u:A\to B$ over $C$ lies in $W$ whenever $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ lies in $W$ for every $c\in C$. Consequently no argument using relative Theorem~A is an argument from the literal absolute Loc~(3) alone.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.1, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Literal absolute Loc (3) is not the adopted relative axiom.

statement: Intrinsic fibrations and their unconditional closure properties. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks and let $W$ be invariant under isomorphism of arrows. For $S\in\mathcal M$, let $W_S$ be the inverse image of $W$ under the source functor $\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M$. Define \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*: \mathcal M/B\to\mathcal M/E\text{ sends }W_B\text{ into }W_E\}. \] Thus every test is an arrow $v:T'\to T$ over $B$, with arbitrary structure map $T\to B$, and the tested arrow is $E\times_B T'\to E\times_B T$. This class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback. These assertions require no two-out-of-three axiom. If $W$ is closed under retracts, then so is $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.2, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: No two-out-of-three needed for composition and base-change closure; retract premise explicit.

statement: The coarse, universal, and local relative classes. Suppose $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal L$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition and pullback. For an arrow $u:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal M/S$, put \[ u\in W_S^{\mathcal L}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(X\times_S T\longrightarrow Y\times_S T\bigr)\in W \quad\hbox{for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L. \] Let $W_S^u$ be the same class with all $T\to S$ allowed. Then \[ W_S^u\subseteq W_S^{\mathcal L}\subseteq W_S. \] All three classes contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Their retract closure follows if $W$ has it. These are precisely the relative classes in XII ms.~210 and 220. They must not be confused with the class of universal $W$-equivalences in $\mathcal M$, where the base is the codomain of the arrow being tested.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.3, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Full faithfulness on coefficients need not satisfy two-out-of-three.

statement: What raw reindexing and postcomposition actually preserve. Under the hypotheses of A.3, a map $f:S'\to S$ in $\mathcal L$ induces \[ f^*:(\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L}). \] For every $f:S'\to S$, without assuming $f\in\mathcal L$, postcomposition induces \[ f_\#:(\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L}). \] If $f^*$ also preserves the displayed classes, the ordinary adjunction $f_\#\dashv f^*$ descends to their localizations. For arbitrary $f$, this calculation alone constructs the descended postcomposition functor; it does not construct its right adjoint.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.4, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Raw pullback is proved homotopical only for the stated class; postcomposition works for every map.

statement: The universal saturation of the local test class. Under A.3, define $\widehat{\mathcal L}$ by the following condition on $f:S'\to S$: for every $T\to S$, pullback along $f_T:T\times_S S'\to T$ sends $W_T^{\mathcal L}$ into $W_{T\times_S S'}^{\mathcal L}$. Then $\widehat{\mathcal L}$ contains $\mathcal L$, contains isomorphisms, and is closed under composition and pullback. Moreover \[ W_S^{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=W_S^{\mathcal L} \quad\hbox{for every }S,\qquad \widehat{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=\widehat{\mathcal L}. \] It is the largest composition- and pullback-closed class containing isomorphisms that defines this same family of fine relative classes. This is the corrected, second definition at XII ms.~222; the first definition on that page omits the universal quantifier over $T\to S$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.5, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: The preliminary base-change universal quantifier is indispensable.

statement: The corrected transporter Galois connection. Let $W$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition in a category $\mathcal M$ with pullbacks. Let $A\subseteq W$ contain isomorphisms and be composition-closed, and let $L$ contain isomorphisms and be pullback-closed. Define \[ \begin{split} T_W(A)&=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*\text{ sends every arrow of }A \text{ in }\mathcal M/B\text{ into }W\},\\ K_W(L)&=\{u:X\to Y\in W\mid p^*u\in W \text{ for every }(p:Y'\to Y)\in L\}. \end{split} \] Then $T_W(A)$ contains isomorphisms and is pullback-closed, $K_W(L)$ contains isomorphisms and is composition-closed, and \[ A\subseteq K_W(L)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L\subseteq T_W(A). \] Both operations reverse inclusions; their composites are extensive, monotone, and idempotent. The closed pairs are exchanged by inverse order-reversing bijections. Their extreme pairs are \[ (W^u,\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M),\qquad (W,\operatorname{Fib}_W), \] where $W^u$ means universal equivalences with respect to the codomain of each arrow.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.6, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Right-hand domain requires pullback closure, not composition closure.

statement: The exact composition criterion, II Proposition 6.1. For a closed pair $A=K_W(L)$, $L=T_W(A)$ of A.6, the following conditions are equivalent: $L$ is composition-closed; pullback along every member of $L$ preserves $A$; and $L=\operatorname{Stab}(A)$, where $\operatorname{Stab}(A)=T_A(A)$. Every stabilizer is composition- and pullback-closed. In particular, a transporter into the larger class $W$ is not generally a stabilizer.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.7, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Correct composition criterion for a closed transporter pair.

statement: Transporters need not compose under the hypotheses of II section 6. The claim in the first version of II~(6.2)--(6.5) that $T_W(A)$ automatically belongs to a right-hand domain requiring composition closure is false. A counterexample is the chain category $0<1<2<3$, with $W$ consisting of the identities and $0\to2,0\to3$, and $A$ consisting of the identities and $0\to3$. Here \[ T_W(A)=\operatorname{Mor}([3])\setminus\{1\to3\},\qquad K_WT_W(A)=A. \] Consequently $1\to2$ and $2\to3$ lie in the transporter while their composite does not.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.8, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: W is composition-closed but not two-out-of-three, exactly as permitted in II section 6.

statement: The meaning of smooth and proper in the manuscript. For a fundamental localizer on $\mathrm{Cat}$, let $\operatorname{As}_W$ consist of $u:A\to B$ for which $A/b\to e$ lies in $W$ for every $b$, and let $\operatorname{Coas}_W$ consist of $u$ for which $b\backslash A\to e$ lies in $W$ for every $b$. The definitions used at II ms.~66 and explicitly reaffirmed at ms.~89 are \[ \operatorname{Liss}_W=\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{As}_W), \qquad \operatorname{Prop}_W=\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{Coas}_W). \] The two mixed transporters contain both the corresponding stabilizer and $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. Neither is the definition of smoothness or properness. The proposed inclusion $\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$ at XII ms.~225--226 is explicitly qualified by ``peut-\^etre'' and is an extra proposed axiom, not a consequence asserted to have been proved there.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.9, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Smooth/proper are asphericity stabilizers, not the mixed transporters into W.

statement: The three fibre axioms, with their quantifiers. For every $S\in\mathcal M$ let $\mathcal F_S$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal M/S$ on the intrinsic fibrations. The three assertions at XII ms.~215--218 are \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{(a)}&\quad J_S:\mathcal F_S[(W_S^u)^{-1}] \longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}]\text{ is an equivalence};\\ \mathrm{(b)}&\quad W_S^u=W_S\text{ on }\mathcal F_S;\\ \mathrm{(c)}&\quad\mathcal F_S[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow \mathcal H[W_S^{-1}]\longrightarrow(\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}] \text{ are equivalences} \end{aligned} \] for every full $\mathcal F_S\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal M/S$. Axiom (a) implies equality of the strong saturations of $W_S^u$ and $W_S$ on $\mathcal F_S$. It does not by that argument imply equality of the original classes. Axioms (b) and (c) imply (a).
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.10, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Axiom a gives equality of strong saturations; b is equality of the original restricted classes.

statement: Enough intrinsic fibrations implies the exact fibrewise invariance. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has pullbacks, $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three, and every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\operatorname{Fib}_W$. Then axiom (b) of A.10 holds, and \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W\cap W=W^u. \] No terminal object, accessibility, functorial factorization, or strong saturation is required for these conclusions.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.11, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: No chosen functorial factorization or terminal object needed.

statement: A functorial replacement proves every intermediate-subcategory comparison. Let $\mathcal A$ be a category with a class $W$ containing isomorphisms and satisfying two-out-of-three, let $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal A$ be full, and suppose there is $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal F$ with a natural transformation $\eta:1_{\mathcal A}\to iR$ whose components are in $W$. For every full $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal A$, both inclusions induce equivalences \[ \mathcal F[W^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal H[W^{-1}] \longrightarrow\mathcal A[W^{-1}]. \] In particular, such slice replacements into $\operatorname{Fib}_W S$, together with enough intrinsic fibrations, verify XII (a), (b), and (c).
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.12, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Sufficient extra replacement hypothesis, not proof from a and b alone.

statement: The implication asked in audit row XIIc B062. The axioms (a) and (b) of A.10, even imposed at every base, do not imply (c). There is a counterexample with six objects, all finite limits and colimits, and strongly saturated $W$. It also refutes the analogous assertion for enhanced localizations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.13, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Six-object finite lattice refutes a+b implies c at every-base scope; W strongly saturated; enhanced version also fails.

statement: The two fine axiom systems in XII ms.225--227. Suppose classes $L,P\subseteq\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M$ contain isomorphisms and are closed under composition and pullback. Define $W_S^g=W_S^L$ and $W_S^d=W_S^P$. The clause called (a) on ms.~226, asserting preservation of $W^g$ by $L$-base change and of $W^d$ by $P$-base change, follows formally from the closure hypotheses. The clause called (b) on that page is the additional pair of assertions \[ \begin{aligned} (L/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^d)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^d\text{ on }L/S,\\ (P/S)[(W_S^u)^{-1}]&\simeq(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^g)^{-1}], &W_S^u=W_S^g\text{ on }P/S. \end{aligned} \] Here $L/S$ and $P/S$ denote full subcategories on the corresponding structural maps. Under these additional equivalences, each fine theory is a contravariant pseudofunctor on all of $\mathcal M$. This conclusion does not require $L\cap P\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.14, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: The c of ms.227 is an adjunction axiom, different from c of ms.218.

statement: The four fibration classes and Loc (7), with reference localizer. For a fundamental localizer $W$, the four classes in XVI section~4 are distinct definitions. Besides intrinsic $\operatorname{Fib}_W$, one has Grothendieck fibrations; $\operatorname{Fib}^{\mathrm{weak}}_W$, tested by all arrows $T'\to T$ over the base with $T'$ and $T$ contractible in the category-homotopy sense; and $\operatorname{Parf}_W=\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W$. Here category-homotopy contractibility means that the identity functor is connected to a constant functor by a finite zigzag of natural transformations. It implies weak contractibility of the nerve, but replacing the test family by all weakly contractible nerves is a separate assertion, not the literal definition. Let $\mathcal G_W$ denote Grothendieck fibrations all of whose transport functors lie in $W$. For any arrow class $\mathcal F$, define \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm A(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W,\\ \mathrm B(\mathcal F)&:\quad W_S\cap\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F/S) \subseteq W_S^u\quad\hbox{for every }S,\\ \mathrm C(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\cap W\subseteq W^u. \end{aligned} \] Loc~(7a), (7b), and (7c) are respectively $\mathrm A(\mathcal G_W)$, $\mathrm B(\mathcal G_W)$, and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G_W)$. For a reference localizer $V\subseteq W$, the conditions $\mathrm A_V,\mathrm B_V,\mathrm C_V$ replace $\mathcal G_W$ by $\mathcal G_V$. The condition $\mathrm D_V$ is $\mathrm A(\operatorname{Parf}_V)$, or its equivalent B and C forms once the hypotheses of A.17 are verified. Loc~(7F) is the factorization condition of A.11, not the inclusion of any one of these reference classes in $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.15, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Four fibration notions and eight reference/factorization variants kept separate.

statement: The implications A to B to C and replacement transfer. Let $W$ and $\mathcal M$ satisfy A.11's initial assumptions. If every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. If identities lie in $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. Suppose that each $p:X\to S$ in $\mathcal F$ admits a comparison $j_p:X\to R_p$ over $S$ in $W_S^u$, with $R_p\to S$ in $\mathcal G$. Then $\mathrm A(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. If for every map $h:X\to Y$ over $S$ between $\mathcal F$-objects the chosen comparisons extend to a commutative square $R(h)j_X=j_Yh$, then also $\mathrm B(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. Functorial replacements suffice; the proof only needs these individual commuting squares.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.16, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Replacement transfer in B needs commuting squares; functoriality suffices.

statement: The full Brown implication with all its premises. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has a terminal object and pullbacks, and $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal F$ contain isomorphisms and all terminal maps, be closed under composition and pullback, and admit a factorization of every arrow as a $W$-map followed by an $\mathcal F$-map. Then \[ \mathrm A(\mathcal F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm B(\mathcal F)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mathrm C(\mathcal F). \] This is the precise abstract assertion of XVI Lemma~4.4.3. The terminal-map premise is part of the statement, not a consequence of an arbitrary intrinsic-fibration factorization.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.17, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Complete relative mapping-path proof, with all terminal-map premises.

statement: The weak constant-coefficient notion does not compose. The universal weak rational cohomological fibrations of I ms.~117--118 need not be closed under composition. The failure occurs for finite categories. Consequently that notion cannot be silently substituted for the intrinsic class in A.2 or for the class in Loc~(7F).
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.18, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Finite covering/opfibration counterexample independently reconstructed.

statement: The local-coefficient repair has an asymmetric conclusion. Let $\mathbb D$ be a derivator in presheaf variance. Suppose that for $p:E\to B$, after every strict base change, the right direct image of every constant coefficient is locally constant and its value at each base object is canonically the right Kan extension from the strict fibre. If $v:T'\to T$ over $B$ is fully faithful on locally constant $\mathbb D$-coefficients, then the pullback $w:E\times_BT'\to E\times_BT$ is a constant-coefficient $\mathbb D$-equivalence. This argument does not assert full faithfulness or an equivalence on all locally constant coefficients upstairs. If the same direct-image and base-change hypothesis is required for every locally constant coefficient on every base-changed total category, then the resulting cohomological-fibration class is closed under composition and pullback. The corresponding statements for left Kan extensions and homology follow by duality.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.19, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Weak constant-coefficient conclusion distinguished from all local systems.

statement: Properness does not imply local constancy of fibres. The inclusion $j:\{1\}\to[1]$ is proper in Grothendieck's presheaf convention, but its comma transition over $0\to1$ is $\varnothing\to e$. Thus the assertion about proper maps at I ms.~102, companion row Ib-C003, is false already for spaces and set coefficients.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.20, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I ms.102; Ib-C003; GALOIS D.9; STRATA D.5
notes: Proper cosieve has comma transition empty to point.

statement: Finite products and the one-fibrant-leg pullback comparison. Assume the hypotheses of A.11 and slice replacement equivalences as in A.12. In the localized fibrant slice over $S$, the product of $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ is represented by $X\times_S Y\to S$. Arbitrary derived reindexing preserves these finite products. Moreover, if $X\to S$ is intrinsic and $Y\to\overline Y\to S$ is a replacement with $Y\to\overline Y\in W$ and $\overline Y\to S$ intrinsic, then $X\times_S Y\to X\times_S\overline Y$ lies in $W$. Thus a strict pullback with one intrinsic leg computes the same relative homotopy object as replacing the other leg first. These are the formal assertions at XII ms.~241--248.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.21, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Finite product universal property proved by localizing the product/diagonal adjunction.

statement: The intrinsic factorization content of the weak Quillen axioms. The conditions M2, M$'$, and M$''$ of XIII ms.~8 imply both intrinsic factorizations: every arrow factors as an intrinsic cofibration followed by a $W$-map, and as a $W$-map followed by an intrinsic fibration. They consequently imply the universal-equivalence equalities of XIII Corollary~1, ms.~10, and the fibrewise assertion of XIII Proposition~4, ms.~10--11. They do not identify the designated classes $TC,TF$ with $C\cap W,F\cap W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.22, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Historical exactness W=TF composed TC is distinguished from one-sided equality.

statement: The variance assertions of XIII section 4 are lifting adjunctions. Let $\mathcal M(I)=\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal M)$, suppose the ordinary Kan extensions used below exist, and let the two closed lifting pairs be $(C(I),TF(I))$ and $(TC(I),F(I))$, with $C(I),TC(I)$ defined objectwise. For $u:I'\to I$ one has \[ u^*C(I)\subseteq C(I'),\quad u^*TC(I)\subseteq TC(I'), \quad u_*F(I')\subseteq F(I),\quad u_*TF(I')\subseteq TF(I), \] and \[ \begin{split} u^*F(I)\subseteq F(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!TC(I')\subseteq TC(I),\\ u^*TF(I)\subseteq TF(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!C(I')\subseteq C(I). \end{split} \] If every component of $i\backslash I'$ has an initial object and the relevant coproducts exist, then all four containments in the last two equivalences hold. In particular injective fibrant diagrams are objectwise fibrant. For a walking-arrow diagram $X_0\leftarrow X_1$, injective fibrancy is equivalent to $X_0$ fibrant and $X_1\to X_0\in F$; this also implies that $X_1$ is fibrant.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.23, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Presheaf variance fixes comma orientation and walking-arrow fibrancy.

statement: Ordinary Kan extensions do not automatically descend. For $(\mathrm{Cat},W_\infty)$, ordinary limits of finite diagrams need not preserve objectwise weak equivalences. Thus an ordinary $u_*$ in XIII ms.~45--50 cannot be identified with a derived $u_*$ without a derivability or fibrancy argument.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.24, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Ordinary limit of an objectwise weak equivalence may fail to be weak.

statement: The noetherian sober Alexandrov qualification adds no infinite posets. If a poset with its Alexandrov topology is noetherian and sober, the poset is finite. Hence the apparently more general admissibility qualification in XIII ms.~60--61, requiring the Alexandrov space of $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ to be noetherian and sober, introduces no genuinely infinite poset beyond the finite case.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.25, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
depends_on: Alexandrov closed sets; infinite Ramsey theorem
notes: Noetherian and sober Alexandrov posets are finite; companion observation independently verified.

statement: The intrinsic finite floor does not provide all small Kan extensions. Finite limits, finite colimits, two-out-of-three, and both intrinsic factorization axioms do not imply existence of all small homotopy Kan extensions. A counterexample is the category of finite sets with isomorphisms as $W$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.26, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
depends_on: finite-set product and coproduct universal properties
notes: Finite intrinsic floor does not imply infinite Kan extensions.

statement: Closedness upgrades historical exactness to both trivial-class equalities. Let $(C,TC,F,TF)$ satisfy the weak Quillen axioms of XIII ms.~27--28, including two-out-of-three for $W$, the two factorizations, and $TC\subseteq C\cap W$, $TF\subseteq F\cap W$. If both lifting pairs are closed and $W=TF\circ TC$, then \[ TC=C\cap W,\qquad TF=F\cap W. \] Moreover $W$ is retract-closed. With the finite limits and colimits of M0 these data are a closed model structure in the original finite-limit convention. The two intrinsic containments M$''$ make this structure proper. Thus a \emph{closed exact} structure, as required by the uniform hypothesis at XIII ms.~57, is stronger than the unqualified exact structure distinguished in A.22.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.27, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Closedness plus exactness DOES imply both trivial-class equalities; the added premise is essential.

statement: The uniform theorem of XIII and the exact admissibility hypothesis. Assume exactly the uniform-left hypothesis of XIII ms.~57: for every $I$ in the specified diagram domain, the objectwise classes $C(I),TC(I)$ and their right orthogonals $TF(I),F(I)$ form a closed exact weak Quillen structure for the objectwise class $W(I)$. Let $u:I'\to I$ be a functor in the domain for which the ordinary presheaf right Kan extension $u_*$ exists. Then $u_*$ preserves weak equivalences between fibrant diagrams. It consequently induces a right adjoint \[ u^*: \mathcal M(I)[W(I)^{-1}] \rightleftarrows\ \mathcal M(I')[W(I')^{-1}]:\mathbf R u_*. \] If the comma categories $I'/i$ and their inclusions into $I'$ belong to the diagram domain, the canonical pointwise formula is \[ i^*\mathbf R u_*X\ \cong\ \mathbf R\!\lim_{(I'/i)^{\mathrm{op}}}X|_{I'/i}. \] In particular every functor between finite posets is admissible under the source's hypotheses. No restriction to finite posets is necessary for admissibility once the relevant ordinary Kan extension and uniform diagram structures exist. In the historical numbering, this proves the right-hand Der~4 and Der~5 assertions of XIII ms.~61; these numbers do not mean modern Der~4 and strongness Der~5.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.28, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
depends_on: A.17,A.23,A.25,A.27; Quillen 1967 I.1 Theorem 1 and I.4 Theorem 3
notes: All u with existing ordinary Kan extension are admissible under the actual uniform closed exact premise.

statement: The polarity calculation in II section 5 requires closure after a join. For any relation $R\subseteq P\times Q$, the maps $A\mapsto A^\perp=\{q\mid pRq\text{ for all }p\in A\}$ and its transpose define an antitone Galois connection on the power sets. Double orthogonality is an extensive idempotent closure; closed subsets are closed under arbitrary intersections, and their join is the closure of their union. If $P,Q$ are complete posets and the principal-polar condition (D$_0$) of II ms.~69 holds, write $c$ for the induced closure on $P$. For a subset $A\subseteq P$, its polar closure is the principal lower set \[ A^{\perp\perp}=\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee A\right) =\mathord\downarrow c\!\left(\bigvee_{a\in A}c(a)\right). \] The final closure cannot be omitted from II formula~(5.20), ms.~76. One must also distinguish the element $c(\bigvee A)$ of $P$ from its principal lower set, a subset of $P$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.29, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: The final closure on the supremum and the distinction element/principal lower set are required.

statement: Arbitrary unions do not preserve composition closure. The class of arrow classes containing identities and closed under both pullback and composition is not closed under arbitrary unions, contrary to the preliminary lattice description in II ms.~65--67. Intersections have that property; a join requires taking the closure of the union under the specified operations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.30, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: A union of composition-closed pullback-closed classes need not compose.

statement: The bi-site remark fixes a question rather than a general theorem. At VI ms.~81--84 the data $(\mathcal M,W)$ specify the coarse slice localization, but the proposed fine classes require additional test data. The two comma tests in $\mathrm{Cat}$ have opposite variances: $X/s$ varies covariantly with $s$, and $s\backslash X$ contravariantly. In XII ms.~222 the class labelled $W^g$ uses the former tests and its universal preservation class is the smooth class discussed in Part B; XII ms.~224's $W^d$ uses the latter. The letters on an earlier page are not a substitute for this variance check. The remark that weak globular infinity-groupoids might have no useful localization theory is a suggestion at VI ms.~83--84. It is not a nonexistence theorem about fine relative theories. The attached 2026 claims about higher categories and globular groupoids remain ``claimed (OpenAI, 2026, unrefereed)'' here \citep{OpenAI2026Thomason,OpenAI2026Groupoids}; no conclusion of Part A depends on either.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.31, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Higher-category 2026 claims not used as proof inputs.

statement: The literal absolute package does not imply relative Theorem A. The literal axioms Loc~(1,2,3) of XVI, with the moderate saturation of A.1, do not imply Loc~(3 bis). The failure already occurs in a triangle of finite groupoids over the one-object category $BC_2$. Thus the absolute package left undecided in POLES A.16 must be distinguished from the relative package used throughout the present paper.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.32, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Component-dependent class satisfies literal moderate saturation and absolute A but fails relative A over BC2. It is not closed under all arrow retracts.

statement: The converse cocartesian assertion of XII ms.274 needs conservativity. Theorem~3$^\circ$ of XII ms.~274 is false without the conservativity premise introduced in its part~2$^\circ$. The assertion that for a map of homotopy cocartesian squares $f_0,f_3\in W$ imply $f_1,f_2\in W$ fails even when $W$ is strongly saturated and the intrinsic cofibration factorization exists. Corollary~1 on that page is also false without that extra premise.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.33, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Strongly saturated isomorphisms on finite sets refute the converse and the unqualified corollary.

statement: Stabilizers alone do not define the antitone correspondence of the cancelled section. For arbitrary arrow classes $A$, the operation $A\mapsto\operatorname{Stab}(A)$ is not antitone. Thus the first, cancelled proposal in II section~4 cannot be used in place of the corrected transporter construction in section~6.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, A.34, statement and following argument; sections/A.tex
notes: Stabilizers are not antitone for arbitrary input classes.

statement: The comma tests and their variance. For a fundamental localizer $W$ and a small category $S$, put \[ \begin{aligned} W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S&=\{u:X\to Y\text{ over }S:\ s\backslash u\in W\text{ for all }s\in S\},\\ W^{\mathrm{co}}_S&=\{u:X\to Y\text{ over }S:\ u/s\in W\text{ for all }s\in S\}. \end{aligned} \] Both are weakly saturated classes contained in the total class $W_S$. Opposition gives an isomorphism of relative categories $(\Cat/S,W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S)\cong (\Cat/S^{\op},W^{\mathrm{co}}_{S^{\op}})$. For $W=W_\infty$, their enhanced localizations are, respectively, $\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces)$ and $\Fun(NS,\Spaces)$. The value of the first classifier at $s$ is $B(s\backslash X)$; the value of the second is $B(X/s)$. In the notation of XII ms.~222, $W^{\mathrm g}_S$ is the second class.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.1, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Presheaf test is s\X; covariant test is X/s.

statement: The simplicial slice test, with the necessary base hypothesis. Let $S$ be a small quasicategory and let $u:X\to Y$ be any map of simplicial sets over $S$; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed fibrant. Then $u$ is a covariant equivalence exactly when \[ X\times_S S_{/s}\longrightarrow Y\times_S S_{/s} \] is a weak homotopy equivalence for every vertex $s$. Replacing $S_{/s}$ by $S_{s/}$ gives the contravariant test. For an arbitrary simplicial base these statements hold with a right, respectively left, fibrant replacement $\widetilde S_{/s}\to S$, respectively $\widetilde S_{s/}\to S$, of the vertex map in place of the literal slice.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.2, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: All total objects allowed; literal slices require a quasicategorical base.

statement: Nerve comparison as an equivalence of enhanced localizations. For every small ordinary category $S$, the ordinary nerve induces equivalences \[ (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{co}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq (\sSet/NS)[(W^{\mathrm{cov}})^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS,\Spaces), \] and, by opposition, \[ (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq (\sSet/NS)[(W^{\mathrm{contra}})^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces). \] Here $W=W_\infty$. These are equivalences of infinity-categories and therefore of homotopy categories. The last comparison is implemented by the straightening--unstraightening Quillen equivalence. No model structure on $\Cat/S$ with the ordinary nerve as a right Quillen functor is asserted.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.3, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Enhanced localization equivalence; no unsupported Quillen claim for the raw nerve.

statement: The literal slice recipe over every simplicial base. Lead~1 is false for arbitrary simplicial bases when its tests use literal simplicial slices. Let $S=\Lambda^2_1$, with nondegenerate edges $01$ and $12$ and no $02$ edge. The map $\{0\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{\{0,1\}}$ over $S$ is a covariant equivalence, but its pullback along $S_{/2}\to S$ is $\varnothing\to\{1\}$ and is not a weak homotopy equivalence.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.4, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Explicit inner-horn base; finite simplex intersections checked.

statement: The exact dictionary for smoothness and properness. For $p:A\to B$ in $\Cat$, Grothendieck's $W_\infty$-properness is equivalent to properness of $Np$ in \citet[Definition 4.4.1]{BCCisinski2019}, and to smoothness of $Np$ in \citet[Definition 4.1.2.9]{DGLurieHTT}. Grothendieck's $W_\infty$-smoothness corresponds to Cisinski-smoothness and to the opposite of Lurie's smoothness. Thus the two cited books use opposite names. The equivalences hold in both directions for all ordinary functors, without a fibration hypothesis.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.5, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Grothendieck-proper equals Lurie-smooth; ordinary nerve criterion unaffected by erratum.

statement: The maximal localization class, for every fundamental localizer. Let $\widehat{\mathcal L}_{\mathrm{co}}$ consist of those $p:A\to B$ for which every strict base change $p_T:A\times_BT\to T$ preserves $W^{\mathrm{co}}_T$ under raw pullback. Then \[ \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\mathrm{co}}=\Liss_W, \qquad \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\mathrm{pre}}=\Prop_W. \] No accessibility assumption is needed. In particular the equality left open at XII ms.~222 has an affirmative answer in the manuscript's covariant variance; it is not the assertion that all raw inverse images are homotopical.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.6, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Maximal class equality settled with covariant manuscript variance, without accessibility.

statement: Three different fibration classes at the minimal localizer. There are strict inclusions \[ \{\text{Grothendieck bifibrations}\}\subsetneq \Liss_{W_\infty}\cap\Prop_{W_\infty}\subsetneq\Fib_{W_\infty}. \] For simplicial sets, Cisinski-smooth and Cisinski-proper maps likewise lie in the intrinsic class preserving all weak homotopy equivalences under strict pullback. The analogous inclusion for a larger fundamental localizer is generally false.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.7, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Diamond and V finite separators; strict pullback class distinguished from bifibrations.

statement: An explicit smooth and proper path resolution. For a small category $C$ and $x\in C$, let $E_x(C)$ have as objects the functors $\gamma:J\to C$, where $J$ has objects $\mathbb Z$ and arrows $2i\to2i-1$, $2i\to2i+1$, which are constantly $x$ with identity arrows at the left end and constantly some object at the right end. Morphisms are natural transformations whose eventual left component is $1_x$; composition is componentwise. Then $q:E_x(C)\to C$, taking the eventual right value, is $W_\infty$-smooth and proper, $BE_x(C)$ is weakly contractible, and its strict fibres are the homotopy fibres of $\{x\}\to BC$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.8, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Fully specified integer-fence category; all lift contractions proved.

statement: The exact localizer threshold for complementarity. For a fundamental localizer $W$ in the relative-Theorem-A convention, \[ \Liss_W\cap\Prop_W\subset\Fib_W \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad W=W_\infty\ \text{or}\ W=\operatorname{Mor}(\Cat). \] Accessibility is not required. Thus the tentative complementarity at XII ms.~225--226 is false for every proper enlargement of $W_\infty$ other than the total class.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.9, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms.225--226; POLES E.5; STRATA G.5
notes: Only minimal and total localizers; no accessibility.

statement: Complementarity for every finite truncation localizer. For every $n\geq0$, $\Liss_{W_n}\cap\Prop_{W_n}$ is not contained in $\Fib_{W_n}$. For $n=0$ a finite witness is the regular covering $EC_2\to BC_2$. For $n\geq1$ B.8 supplies a completely specified witness with base the face poset of the boundary of an $(n+2)$-simplex.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.10, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms.225--226; POLES C.8--C.9; STRATA G.3--G.4
notes: W0 finite covering; all finite truncations by specified sphere path model.

statement: A single covering refutes complementarity for every nonzero homology theory. Let $E$ be any nonzero spectrum, with no connectivity assumption, and let $W_E$ mean equivalence on $E\wedge\Sigma^\infty(-)_+$. The three-sheeted action-groupoid covering in the prompt is both $W_E$-smooth and $W_E$-proper, but is not in $\Fib_{W_E}$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.11, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms.225--226; POLES C.10; PATHS E.9
notes: One covering and one free-group endomorphism work for every nonzero spectrum, including nonconnective spectra.

statement: A finite bifibration defeats both $W_1$ and rational local-system equivalences. Put $W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_{D(\mathbb Q)}^{\mathrm{lc}}$, where locally constant diagrams are coherent diagrams of unbounded rational complexes. There is a finite bifibration $p:H\to K$, with $14$ objects and $100$ arrows upstairs, which belongs to both $\Liss_W\cap\Prop_W$ for every fundamental localizer $W$, but belongs to neither $\Fib_{W_1}$ nor $\Fib_{W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$. The functor $p$ itself belongs to $W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.12, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Finite gerbe and self-pullback; exact nonabelian group presentations checked.

statement: The covering witnesses have different behaviour for local coefficients. Every covering of ordinary categories, meaning a discrete fibration and a discrete opfibration, belongs to $\Fib_{W_1}$ and to $\Fib_{W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$. In particular the three-sheeted covering of B.11 belongs to these two intrinsic classes, although it belongs to no $\Fib_{W_E}$ for $E\ne0$. The endpoint map of B.8 with $C=BC_2$ lies in the same two intrinsic classes, while it fails to lie in the rational-homology intrinsic class.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.13, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: GALOIS D.3; POLES C.10; PATHS E.9
notes: Coverings preserve W1 and rational local-system equivalences, unlike all homology localizers.

statement: Cohomological fibrations are not the proper class. Let $\mathcal D$ be the derivator of a nonterminal presentable infinity-category, and use presheaf variance. Define a cohomological $\mathcal D$-fibration by requiring, after every strict base change, that right Kan extension sends every locally constant coefficient to a locally constant coefficient and has the canonical strict-fibre formula. This class and $\Prop_{W_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$ are not contained in one another. Dually, the homological class and $\Liss_{W_{\mathcal D}^{\mathrm{lc}}}$ are not contained in one another. In particular both conclusions apply to sets, spaces, and rational complexes.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.14, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I ms.117--118; GALOIS D.2 and D.9
notes: Neither containment for proper versus strong cohomological, and dually.

statement: Disposition of the inherited finite coefficient examples. The following table evaluates the maps specified in GALOIS D.3--D.5 for $W=W_1$ and $W=W_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}$. A pair of entries gives these two localizers in that order; a single entry applies to both. Here ``smooth'' and ``proper'' always use the same $W$ as the intrinsic column. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{specified map}&W\text{-smooth}&W\text{-proper}&\Fib_W\\\hline \mathrm{D.3}:p:E\to B&\text{yes}&\text{yes}&\text{yes}\\ \mathrm{D.3}:q:B\to[1]&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.3}:qp&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.4}:p:E\to B&\text{yes}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.4}:q:B\to[1]&\text{no}&\text{yes}&(\text{yes},\text{no})\\ \mathrm{D.4}:qp&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.5}:H\to K&\text{yes}&\text{yes}&\text{no}\\ \mathrm{D.5}:q:R\to[1]&\text{no}&\text{yes}&\text{no} \end{array} \]
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.15, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Every named finite map tested for W1 and rational locally constant complexes.

statement: Accessible coefficient localizations and the limit of the general statement. If $W$ is an accessible fundamental localizer, let $\Spaces_W$ be the presentable localization of spaces corresponding to $W$. Then \[ (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{pre}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces_W),\qquad (\Cat/S)[(W^{\mathrm{co}}_S)^{-1}]_\infty \simeq\Fun(NS,\Spaces_W). \] For an arbitrary fundamental localizer the relative definitions, the opposition isomorphism, B.6 and B.9 remain valid without accessibility. A presentable coefficient category in the displayed formulas is not asserted without the accessibility hypothesis.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.16, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Accessible coefficient presentation; no presentability claimed for arbitrary inaccessible W.

statement: Intrinsic fibrations for truncation localizers. For $n\geq0$, a functor $p:T\to B$ lies in $\Fib_{W_n}$ if and only if, for every $X\to B$, the canonical map \[ \tau_{\leq n}B(T\times_BX)\longrightarrow \tau_{\leq n}BT\times_{\tau_{\leq n}BB}\tau_{\leq n}BX \] is an equivalence of $n$-types. The pullback on the right is a homotopy pullback in $\Spaces_{\leq n}$. For $n=0$ this is equivalent to the following elementary pair of conditions. For every connected component $B_j$ of $B$, write $T_j=T\times_BB_j$. Then $\pi_0(T_b)\to\pi_0(T_j)$ must be bijective for each $b\in B_j$; and for every arrow $\beta:b\to b'$ and every component $c$ of $T_j$ there must be an arrow of $T$ over $\beta$ in component $c$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.17, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Proper-localizer hypothesis explicitly verified; elementary W0 criterion also proved.

statement: Useful bounds for a homology intrinsic class. For every spectrum $E$, $\Fib_{W_E}$ contains product projections and inclusions of unions of connected components, together with their closure under composition, strict base change and retracts. It is contained in the class of $p:T\to B$ for which every inclusion \[ T_{\sigma(i)}\longrightarrow T\times_B[m], \qquad \sigma:[m]\to B,quad 0\leq i\leq m, \] is an $E$-equivalence. For $E\ne0$ this upper bound is strict.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.18, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Bounds for intrinsic homology fibrations; simplex tests insufficient.

statement: The full fence construction and its mapping-path factorization. Let $\mathcal P(C)$ be the category of all eventually constant diagrams $J\to C$ on the integer fence of B.8, with all natural transformations. Write $\sigma,\beta$ for the eventual left and right values. Then $(\sigma,\beta):\mathcal P(C)\to C\times C$ is smooth and proper for $W_\infty$, and therefore for every fundamental localizer. For every $f:A\to C$, the functors \[ E(f)=A\times_{C,\sigma}\mathcal P(C),\qquad i_f(a)=(a,\operatorname{const}_{f(a)}),\qquad p_f(a,\gamma)=\beta(\gamma) \] give $f=p_fi_f$, with $i_f\in W_\infty$ and $p_f$ smooth and proper. All formulas are natural in strictly commuting squares. For $C=[1]$, the endpoint functor is neither a Grothendieck fibration nor an opfibration. Thus the verified fence construction in PATHS has exactly the asserted homotopical properties, without being a bifibration.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.19, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Independent all-ended fence proof and functorial factorization; not a strict bifibration.

statement: Reversing path words does not repair the all-type endpoint functor. Use the all-type category $\operatorname{Ch}(C)$ with objects finite oriented interval diagrams and morphisms $(h,\eta)$, where $h$ is an endpoint-preserving, weakly monotone functor of their interval types and $\eta:\gamma\Rightarrow\delta h$. Its endpoint map is smooth for every $C$, but for $C=[1]$ it is not proper and is neither a Grothendieck opfibration nor a fibration. The conclusion cannot be transferred from B.19 by calling both objects ``path categories'' or by reversing the path word.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.20, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: Smoothness proved by padding and contractible slice; empty outgoing lift and two incoming type maps refute stronger claims.

statement: Replacing a smooth and proper representative by a bifibration. For the one-object category of the monoid $R=\{1,e_{00},e_{01},e_{10},e_{11}\}$ with $e_{ij}e_{kl}=e_{il}$ and $1r=r1=r$, it remains unsettled here whether the local system of path spaces has a representative by a strict Grothendieck bifibration with contractible total category. The eventual fence endpoint functor is not such a representative.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.21, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: STRATA E.11; PATHS E.6 and E.11
notes: Open only for existence of some alternative bifibration; standard path obstruction checked.

statement: The maximal simplicial classes and the all-base recipe. For every simplicial base $S$, let $W^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$ and $W^{\mathrm{contra}}_S$ denote the actual covariant and contravariant equivalences. The maps whose every base change preserves these classes under raw pullback are, respectively, Cisinski-smooth and Cisinski-proper maps. Moreover the manuscript's universal test recipe gives exactly \[ W^{\Liss_{\mathrm{Cis}}}_S=W^{\mathrm{cov}}_S, \qquad W^{\Prop_{\mathrm{Cis}}}_S=W^{\mathrm{contra}}_S. \] Thus opposition gives a perfect duality over $S^{\op}$ for every simplicial base, although B.4 refutes the version using literal slices at an arbitrary base. For accessible $W$, replace fibrewise equivalences of spaces by fibrewise $W$-equivalences after left or right fibrant replacement. These two accessible localizations classify diagrams with values in $\Spaces_W$ on the directed infinity-category presented by $S$ or its opposite, and their restrictions to ordinary nerves are B.16. Their universal raw-pullback classes contain the minimal smooth and proper classes. Complementarity with intrinsic total $W$-equivalences holds for these classes only for $W_\infty$ and the total localizer.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, B.22, statement and following argument; sections/B.tex
notes: All simplicial bases using true covariant structures; accessible coefficient extension and rigidity.

statement: What a presheaf model supplies before choosing a direction. Let $A$ be any small category, $\widehat A=\operatorname{Set}^{A^{\op}}$, and $i_A X=A/X$ its category of elements. For a fundamental localizer $W$ put $W_A=i_A^{-1}W$. For each $S\in\widehat A$ there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \widehat A/S\cong\operatorname{Set}^{(A/S)^{\op}}. \] There are two specified, weakly saturated classes on this slice obtained from B.1: \[ W^{\mathrm{pre,el}}_S=i_A^{-1}W^{\mathrm{pre}}_{A/S},\qquad W^{\mathrm{co,el}}_S=i_A^{-1}W^{\mathrm{co}}_{A/S}. \] Both are contained in the total class $W_A$ over $S$. These define localizations for any $A$, but test-category theory alone does not identify them with the two simplicial theories of Part~B.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.1, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
notes: Two specified elements-based candidates, not an unstated unique notion.

statement: The two category-of-elements candidates need not be dual, even on a test category. Assume $W\subseteq W_0$. For every small $A$ and $S\in\widehat A$, $W^{\mathrm{pre,el}}_S$ consists exactly of isomorphisms. For $A=\Delta$, $S=1$, and $W=W_\infty$, $W^{\mathrm{co,el}}_1$ is instead the ordinary class of weak homotopy equivalences of simplicial sets. Their enhanced localizations are not equivalent. Thus transporting both fine tests through the category of elements does not give an automatic extension of Part~B to presheaves.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.2, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
notes: Candidate duality fails already on the test category Delta; does not deny directed simplicial opposition.

statement: Elementwise smoothness and properness do not admit a general exchange involution. Define a map $u:X\to Y$ in $\widehat A$ to be elementwise $W$-smooth or $W$-proper when $i_Au:A/X\to A/Y$ has that categorical property. Every presheaf map is elementwise $W$-smooth, for every fundamental localizer. If $W\subseteq W_0$, a map is elementwise $W$-proper exactly when all its naturality squares are pullbacks of sets. Already for the test category $A=\Delta$, no autoequivalence of $\widehat A$ can exchange these two classes.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.3, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
notes: All maps elementwise smooth; proper iff naturality squares cartesian for W subset W0.

statement: The extra structure that does transport a duality. Let $M$ have pullbacks and a weakly saturated class $W$, and let $\mathcal L_+,\mathcal L_-$ be two pullback-stable classes. Suppose $D:M\to M$ is an involutive equivalence preserving $W$, together with its canonical pullback comparisons, and carrying $\mathcal L_+$ to $\mathcal L_-$. Then the universal-test classes satisfy \[ D(W_S^{\mathcal L_+})=W_{DS}^{\mathcal L_-}, \] and $D$ induces an equivalence of the corresponding enhanced slice localizations. It also exchanges their universal raw-pullback-preserving classes. Such data are sufficient; being a test category supplies none of the required exchange isomorphisms by itself.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.4, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
notes: Exact sufficient duality data; changing index to its opposite is distinct from simplex reversal.

statement: Theorem A for the required strict higher slices. For $1\leq n\leq\omega$, write $V^{(n)}$ for strict $n$-functors whose Street nerves are weak homotopy equivalences; this notation is distinct from the truncation localizer $W_n$ of B.10. Use the under-slices of \citet[\S4]{BCAraMaltsiniotis2018} and their total-dual over-slices. For a strictly commuting triangle $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\to S$, either of the conditions \[ s\backslash u\in V^{(n)}\quad(s\in S_0), \qquad\text{or}\qquad u/s\in V^{(n)}\quad(s\in S_0) \] implies $u\in V^{(n)}$. The same result allows the specified oplax triangle in the cited theorem.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.5, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
notes: Opened exact Theorem A references and slice conventions; independent of model claim.

statement: Two strict higher relative theories and a definite duality. For a strict small $n$-category $S$, define $V^{\mathrm{pre}}_S$ and $V^{\mathrm{co}}_S$ by the two slice tests in C.5. They are weakly saturated and contained in the total class $V^{(n)}$. Let $D_{\mathrm{tot}}$ reverse every positive-dimensional cell. Then \[ (n\Cat/S,V^{\mathrm{pre}}_S) \cong(n\Cat/D_{\mathrm{tot}}S,V^{\mathrm{co}}_{D_{\mathrm{tot}}S}) \] as relative categories, and hence their enhanced localizations are equivalent. This conclusion holds for every $1\leq n\leq\omega$ and uses none of the claimed September 2026 model structures.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.6, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
notes: Formal fine duality for every strict dimension, with total-cell reversal.

statement: What replaces the single opposite in strict dimension $n$. For each subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, or $J\subseteq\mathbb N_{>0}$ when $n=\omega$, reversing the $j$-cells for $j\in J$ defines an involutive automorphism $D_J$ of strict $n$-categories and preserves $V^{(n)}$. The generators commute and compose by symmetric difference. Define $\Liss^{(n)}$ to be the maps whose every strict base change preserves $V^{\mathrm{co}}$ under raw pullback, and $\Prop^{(n)}$ using $V^{\mathrm{pre}}$. Then both classes contain isomorphisms and are stable under composition and strict base change; $D_{\mathrm{tot}}$ exchanges them. These definitions alone do not identify them with a higher lifting-category criterion or with smooth/proper Street-nerve maps.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.7, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
notes: All cell dualities and universal preservation definitions; no unproved lifting characterization.

statement: The verified absolute model structure in dimension two. The category of strict $2$-categories has the proper combinatorial Thomason model structure with weak equivalences detected by the Street nerve, and $c_2\operatorname{Sd}^2\dashv\operatorname{Ex}^2N_2$ is a Quillen equivalence with simplicial sets in the Kan--Quillen structure.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.8, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
notes: Verified published dimension-two theorem, not reliance on September 2026 claim.

statement: The exact coarse consequence of an absolute higher model theorem. Suppose, for a fixed $n$, that the model structure and Quillen equivalence claimed in family~317 are valid \citep[claimed, unrefereed]{OpenAI2026Thomason}. Then the total-weak-equivalence localization of $n\Cat/S$ presents $\Spaces_{/|N_nS|}$, the slice of spaces over the classifying space of the Street nerve. It has the usual derived postcomposition and pullback adjunctions. This is a coarse statement. It does not imply recognition of C.6's fine localizations or any universal base-change property for the classes in C.7. For $n=2$ the premise is already verified by C.8.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.9, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
depends_on: C.8 for n=2; conditional OpenAI2026Thomason for n>2
notes: Precise coarse slice consequence only.

statement: The strict higher fine recognition and base-change problem. For a general strict $n$-category $S$, $2\leq n\leq\omega$, the following specific extension is not proved here: the Street nerve induces equivalences from the two enhanced localizations in C.6 to the actual covariant and contravariant localizations over $N_nS$, with the slice conventions matched as in C.5; moreover C.7's preservation classes admit a local higher comma-lifting criterion and satisfy the universal Kan base-change axioms of Part~E. These are required before declaring every such $(n\Cat,V^{(n)},\Liss^{(n)},\Prop^{(n)})$ an instance of the abstract theorem. Accepting family~317 does not remove these requirements.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, C.10, statement and following argument; sections/C.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Recent-results family 317; Parts C and E
notes: Open relative Street-nerve recognition and higher base-change criterion; exact missing comparisons stated.

statement: The actual comparison supplied by open tests. For a space $Y$, put \[ \begin{split} W^{\mathrm{opn}}_Y=\{u:X\longrightarrow X'\text{ over }Y:\quad& \Pi(u^{-1}U):\Pi(X\times_YU)\longrightarrow\Pi(X'\times_YU)\\ &\text{is an equivalence for every open }U\subseteq Y\}. \end{split} \] Here $u^{-1}U$ means the displayed restricted map, not an inverse-image operation on morphisms. This class contains the isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three and retract closure. There is a canonical functor \[ C_Y:(\mathrm{Top}/Y)[(W^{\mathrm{opn}}_Y)^{-1}] \longrightarrow\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal S),\qquad C_Y(X)(U)=\Pi(X\times_YU). \tag{D.1} \] Its values are hypercomplete cosheaves. This statement does not assert that (D.1) is an equivalence for every $Y$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.1, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
notes: Comparison only; no unrestricted realization equivalence asserted

statement: A complete realization theorem for finite Alexandrov bases. Let $P$ be a finite poset with the topology of downsets. There are equivalences \[ (\mathrm{Top}/P)[(W^{\mathrm{opn}}_P)^{-1}] \simeq\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal S) \simeq\operatorname{CoShv}(P;\mathcal S). \tag{D.2} \] The first equivalence sends $f:X\to P$ to the covariant diagram $p\mapsto\Pi f^{-1}(P_{\leq p})$. It includes arbitrary, possibly empty fibres and non-Hausdorff total spaces. For a discrete, possibly infinite base $P$ the same statement holds by decomposition into its open fibres.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.2, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part D Lead 2; STRATA A.1 finite case
notes: Explicit relative adjunction D left adjoint E; all topological total spaces allowed

statement: The two variances are not automatically equivalent unstably. For finite Alexandrov $P$ the sheaf theory is $\operatorname{Shv}(P;\mathcal S)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, whereas D.2 gives the covariant diagram category for open inverse-image tests. These categories need not be equivalent. In particular an unstable sheaf--cosheaf duality for all topological spaces is false.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.3, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
notes: Three-object fork; every candidate anti-isomorphism exhausted by code

statement: Proper maps do not preserve open-test equivalences. Even for locally compact Hausdorff spaces, strict pullback along a proper map need not preserve $W^{\mathrm{opn}}$. Thus geometric proper base change for sheaves cannot be read as this assertion about spaces over a base.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.4, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
notes: LCH example (0 1] into [0 1] pulled back at endpoint 0

statement: Local product maps preserve the open-test class. Suppose $g:Z\to Y$ is locally a projection: each point of $Z$ has an open neighbourhood isomorphic over an open $V\subseteq Y$ to $V\times K\to V$, with $K$ a topological space. Then strict pullback along $g$ sends $W^{\mathrm{opn}}_Y$ to $W^{\mathrm{opn}}_Z$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.5, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
notes: No fibre compactness or contractibility used for this assertion

statement: Proper base change is a coefficient theorem. Consider a cartesian square of locally compact Hausdorff spaces \[ \begin{array}{ccc} X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\[-2pt] {\scriptstyle f'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}\\[-2pt] Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y. \end{array} \] If $f$ is proper, the canonical mate $g^*f_*\to f'_*g'^*$ is an equivalence on sheaves of spaces. It is also an equivalence on sheaves with values in a stable bicomplete infinity-category. These are ordinary infinity-sheaves; hypercompletion is not silently substituted.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.6, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
notes: LCH spaces; spaces or stable bicomplete infinity-category coefficients

statement: A precise smooth topological comparison. A space $K$ is essential when the constant-sheaf functor $\mathcal S\to\operatorname{Shv}(K;\mathcal S)$ has a left adjoint. A shape submersion $g:Z\to Y$ is locally, on its source, a projection $V\times K\to V$ with $V$ open in $Y$ and $K$ essential. Assume either $Y$ is locally compact or all these $K$ are locally compact. Then for any presentable coefficient infinity-category $\mathcal C$ there is an adjunction $g_\sharp\dashv g^*$ on sheaves with these coefficients. In a cartesian square as in D.6 with $g$ a shape submersion and with the same local compactness condition after pullback, the canonical maps \[ g'_\sharp f'^*\longrightarrow f^*g_\sharp, \qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^* \] are equivalences.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.7, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
notes: Essential local fibres and exact local-compactness hypothesis; presentable coefficients

statement: The stable sheaf--cosheaf equivalence and the shriek operation. For a locally compact Hausdorff space $Y$ and a stable bicomplete infinity-category $\mathcal C$, there is an equivalence \[ \mathbb V_Y:\operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathcal C) \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\operatorname{CoShv}(Y;\mathcal C), \qquad \mathbb V_Y(F)(U)= \operatorname*{colim}_{K\subseteq U\ { m compact}} \operatorname{fib}\bigl(F(Y)\to F(Y\setminus K)\bigr). \tag{D.8} \] For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ between such spaces, cosheaf pushforward $f_+$ is $(f_+G)(U)=G(f^{-1}U)$. The topological operation with proper support is $f_!=\mathbb V_Y^{-1}f_+\mathbb V_X$ and has a right adjoint $f^!$. For proper $f$ it agrees with $f_*$. This does not identify $f_!$ with the left adjoint $f_\sharp$ of D.7.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.8, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
notes: Compactly supported shriek differs from the left adjoint to inverse image

statement: Realization does not turn every Kan extension into a geometric direct image. Under the least-vertex stratification, categorical properness and properness of a realized finite-poset map are different. Ambient topological direct image need not preserve the least-vertex constructible sheaves and need not equal categorical right Kan extension.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.9, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: STRATA D.5 D.8; Part D geometric dictionary
notes: Endpoint inclusion into interval gives constant Kan extension versus nonconstructible skyscraper

statement: A geometric class on which the categorical comparison is literal. For finite posets equipped with their least-vertex models, closed cosieve inclusions and product projections have topological direct images equal to their categorical right Kan extensions for space, spectrum, and derived-ring coefficients. A sieve is represented by the open complement of the complementary cosieve, rather than in general by the inclusion of its own nerve. These assertions use the finite-poset exodromy comparison, as verified in G.10 below.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.10, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: STRATA D.8; Part D specified positive class
notes: Sieve represented by open complement and minimum-preserving deformation retraction

statement: The realization comparison for every proper map of finite posets. Let $f:P\to Q$ be a $W_\infty$-proper map of finite posets. Equivalently, for every $p\in P$ and $q\geq f(p)$ the outgoing lifting poset \[ L(p,q)=\{r\in P:r\geq p,\ f(r)=q\} \tag{D.11a} \] is weakly contractible. With the minimum stratifications, the topological direct image $|Nf|_*$ preserves constructibility and identifies with the categorical $f_*$, including its adjunction data. This holds for spaces, spectra, and the derived category of modules over any ring. Thus the requested geometric class contains the realizations of all such proper functors, with the specified constructibility property, although mere topological properness does not suffice by D.9.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.11, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part D requested general realization class
notes: Geometric fibre face-poset minimum functor is homotopy initial by an iterated lifting-poset induction

statement: The unrestricted topological realization and its proposed dual. For a locally compact Hausdorff base $Y$, is the functor $C_Y$ in (D.1), with all topological total spaces allowed, an equivalence? If so, what precise localization of spaces over the same $Y$ presents $\operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathcal S)$ and is compatible with the proposed dual class of base-change maps? Neither statement is established in this audit for a general $Y$; the first unproved test base in our argument is $\mathbb R$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.12, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
notes: First unproved base in argument is R; no missing proof converted to falsity

statement: A specified stable cosheaf counterpart for smooth finite-poset maps. There is a precise geometric dual on finite coefficients which uses the maximum stratification and Verdier transport. Let $\mathcal C$ be spectra or modules over a commutative ring, let $D$ be the coefficient duality on finite spectra or perfect modules, and let $E_P^{\max}:\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)\to \operatorname{Shv}(|NP|;\mathcal C)$ be G.10 for $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. Define the contravariant fully faithful functor \[ \Phi_P(F)=\mathbb V_{|NP|}\,E_P^{\max}(DF), \qquad F\in\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C^{\mathrm{perf}}). \tag{D.13a} \] If $f:P\to Q$ is categorically smooth, then its realization $g$ satisfies \[ \Phi_Q(f_!F)\simeq g_+\Phi_P(F). \tag{D.13b} \] Thus ordinary cosheaf pushforward realizes this specified dual of left Kan extension. The cosheaf subcategories in (D.13a) are defined as Verdier images of maximum-constructible perfect sheaves; they are not being identified with literal minimum-constructible cosheaves. For a noncommutative ring the target coefficients are modules over its opposite ring.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, D.13, statement and following argument; sections/D.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part D dual geometric class for smooth maps
notes: Contravariant coefficient duality followed by maximum-stratum realization and Verdier transport

statement: The formal slice construction. Let $\mathcal M$ be a $\mathbb U$-small category with pullbacks, let $W$ contain the isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three, and let $\mathcal L$ contain the isomorphisms and be stable under composition and pullback. The same assertion holds for a larger category when all the localizations below exist in the chosen larger universe. For $S\in\mathcal M$, put \[ W_S^{\mathcal L}=\{u:X\to Y\text{ in }\mathcal M/S: u\times_S T\in W\text{ for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L\}. \] This class contains isomorphisms, has two-out-of-three, and is contained in $W_S$, the class detected on total objects. If $W$ is closed under retracts, so is $W_S^{\mathcal L}$. Every postcomposition functor $\Sigma_f:\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M/T$, for $f:S\to T$, preserves these classes. If $f\in\mathcal L$, strict pullback $f^{-1}:\mathcal M/T\to\mathcal M/S$ also preserves them and the ordinary adjunction $\Sigma_f\dashv f^{-1}$ descends to both the ordinary and enhanced localizations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.1, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Raw slice adjunction only along the testing class; all postcomposition functors descend.

statement: Arbitrary raw pullback does not follow. The hypotheses of E.1 do not imply that raw pullback preserves the fine classes for every $f$. In the presheaf fine theory of $\Cat/[1]$, the inclusion $u:e_1\to[1]$ over $[1]$ is a fine equivalence, whereas its pullback along $e_0\to[1]$ is $\varnothing\to e$, which is not. Consequently the inverse image on the fine localization, when it exists, cannot in general be computed by raw pullback.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.2, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Exact endpoint counterexample; ef_finite_checks.py.

statement: A recognition theorem giving all three Kan functors. Suppose that the enhanced localizations $\mathscr E(S)=(\mathcal M/S)[(W_S^{\mathcal L})^{-1}]_\infty$ exist for bases $S$ in a category $\mathcal B$. Suppose we are given a functor $C:\mathcal B\to\Cat_\infty$ with small values and fully faithful functors $h_S:C(S)\to\mathscr E(S)$ satisfying the following precise presentation hypotheses. The category $\mathscr E(S)$ has all small colimits. Each functor $\Map(h_S(c),-):\mathscr E(S)\to\Spaces$ preserves all small colimits. These functors jointly detect equivalences. For each $f:S\to T$, postcomposition descends to a colimit-preserving functor $F_f:\mathscr E(S)\to\mathscr E(T)$ and there is a coherent equivalence $F_fh_S\simeq h_TC(f)$. Then the restricted Yoneda functors give equivalences \[ H_S:\mathscr E(S)\simeq\Fun(C(S)^{\op},\Spaces),\qquad H_S(X)(c)=\Map(h_S(c),X). \] Under these equivalences, $F_f$ is left Kan extension along $C(f)^{\op}$; it has right adjoint $f^*$, given by restriction, and this restriction has right adjoint $f_*$. These are coherent functors of the base, hence yield the requested pseudofunctors on homotopy categories. The locally constant subcategory has both adjoints to its inclusion. None of the presentation hypotheses is claimed to follow from E.1 or from factorization through intrinsic fibrations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.3, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Enhanced compact-projective presentation is an explicit extra hypothesis; it is not inferred from enough intrinsic fibrations.

statement: Coefficient localization and exact squares. In E.3 one may replace the coefficient category of spaces by any presentable infinity-category $\mathcal V$, once the slice presentation with those coefficients has been verified. In particular, an accessible reflective localization $L:\Spaces\to\mathcal V$ gives the objectwise localization \[ \Fun(C(S)^{\op},\Spaces)\longrightarrow\Fun(C(S)^{\op},\mathcal V). \] Restriction still has both Kan adjoints, and the locally constant subcategory is reflective and coreflective. For a strictly commuting square of ordinary indexing categories, base change for these Kan functors follows whenever its relevant comma-category comparison is homotopy final for left Kan extension, or homotopy initial for right Kan extension. In particular the presheaf left base-change map is invertible if the vertical map is $W_\infty$-smooth or the horizontal map is $W_\infty$-proper; the right map is invertible with these two roles reversed.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.4, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Presentable coefficient version; canonical mates and exact comma comparisons.

statement: Instances and the extra coarse comparison. For $W_\infty$, the presheaf fine localization of $\Cat/S$ satisfies E.3 with $C(S)=NS$ and $h_S(s)$ the point $e_s\to S$; the dual localization uses $NS^{\op}$. The contravariant and covariant simplicial model structures give the same instances over quasicategorical bases, with the proviso in Part B about raw strict slice tests over arbitrary simplicial sets. For finite Alexandrov posets with downsets open and unrestricted topological total spaces, the open-test localization is the covariant instance $C(P)=NP^{\op}$ proved in Part D. Discrete topological bases give the product of copies of spaces directly. The additional assertion that the coarse localization agrees with the locally constant part requires the coarse comparison \[ (\mathcal M/S)[W_S^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\Spaces_{/BC(S)} \simeq\Fun(BC(S)^{\op},\Spaces) \] and compatibility of its localization functor with $\Lan_{q_S^{\op}}$. For $(\Cat,W_\infty)$ this comparison holds. It is not part of the abstract recognition hypotheses.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.5, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Coarse equals locally constant only after the extra coarse comparison.

statement: The coarse theory is not the locally constant fine theory for every localizer. Replacing $W_\infty$ by an arbitrary fundamental localizer in the coarse comparison of E.5 is false. Already for $W_0$, the component equivalences, and $S=BC_2$, the canonical coarse localization identifies two distinct locally constant objects of the fine theory.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.6, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: BC2 with component equivalences; fine local systems retain a regular action lost by total localization.

statement: What enough intrinsic fibrations supplies. Let $\mathcal M$ have a terminal object and pullbacks, and let $W$ contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Define $\Fib_W$ by universal preservation of $W$ under strict pullback. Assume that every morphism factors as a map in $W$ followed by a map in $\Fib_W$. Then every map in $W\cap\Fib_W$ remains in $W$ after arbitrary pullback. Consequently the full subcategory of objects whose terminal map lies in $\Fib_W$, with these weak equivalences and fibrations, is a category of fibrant objects and presents the same enhanced localization as $\mathcal M$. It supplies finite homotopy limits and the usual homotopy-fibre construction. This does not identify the fine slice theories, and does not imply E.3.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.7, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: XII ms.240–261; XIII ms.7–12; PATHS D.8,D.17,D.18
notes: Brown finite floor; no all-small strict diagram rectification.

statement: The accessible localizers satisfying the intrinsic factorization axiom. For an accessible fundamental localizer $W$ of $\Cat$, factorization through $\Fib_W$ is equivalent to aspherical generation of $W$, to generation by a set of maps $A\to e$, and to right properness of the associated Thomason model structure. In the corresponding accessible localization of spaces it is precisely nullification. Thus truncation localizers satisfy this factorization axiom; the nonzero-spectrum homology localizers in Part B do not. The right class of the associated modality is not the class $\Fib_W$: every $X\to e$ belongs to $\Fib_W$, whereas a terminal map is in that right class only when its fibre is local.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.8, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Necessity of aspherical generation does not use accessibility; model equivalences do.

statement: What a path object must supply. Suppose $\mathcal M$ has finite limits, $W$ has two-out-of-three, and $\mathcal A=\Liss\cap\Prop$ is stable under pullback and composition and contains product projections. Suppose functorially for each $S$ there is a path object \[ S\xrightarrow{c_S}P(S)\xrightarrow{(s_S,t_S)}S\times S, \qquad s_Sc_S=t_Sc_S=\id_S, \] whose endpoint map belongs to $\mathcal A$ and whose source evaluation $s_S$ is universally in $W$. Then every $f:X\to S$ factors functorially as \[ X\xrightarrow{i_f}X\times_{S,s_S}P(S)\xrightarrow{p_f}S \] with $i_f(x)=(x,c_Sf(x))$ in $W$ and $p_f=t_S\pr_2$ in $\mathcal A$. Merely requiring $c_S\in W$ and $(s_S,t_S)\in\mathcal A$ does not prove the required assertion about $i_f$; the transfer hypothesis must be supplied.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.9, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Universal source evaluation is required for the indicated mapping-path transfer.

statement: The groupoid test and the meaning of collapse. Let $S$ be a small groupoid and let $\mathcal M=\mathrm{Gpd}$ with categorical equivalences. For functors of groupoids over $S$, both comma-test classes agree with the total equivalences. Their enhanced localizations consequently agree with the coarse theory, which is the infinity-category of families of $1$-types over $NS$. Both variances are identified by inversion in $S$. This does not mean that every artificially chosen class $\mathcal L$ gives the coarse localization.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.10, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Proved ordinary-groupoid test; no dependence on the unrefereed globular model claim.

statement: The intermediate-subcategory assertion under replacement data. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks, let $W$ contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three, and suppose that every arrow factors as a $W$-map followed by an intrinsic $W$-fibration. Suppose in addition that for every base $S$ there is a functor \[ R_S:\mathcal M/S\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fib}_W S \] and a natural transformation $\eta_S:1_{\mathcal M/S}\to i_SR_S$ whose components are in $W_S$, where $i_S$ denotes the full inclusion. Then XII's axioms (a), (b), and (c), in their exact formulations A.10, hold. In particular, for every full subcategory $\operatorname{Fib}_W S\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal M/S$, both inclusions induce equivalences at the restricted $W_S$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.11, statement and following argument; sections/E_b062.tex
notes: Functorial coaugmented W-replacement proves the stronger intermediate assertion.

statement: A six-object counterexample to XIIc B062. The implication $\mathrm{(a)}+\mathrm{(b)}\Rightarrow\mathrm{(c)}$ of A.10 is false, even for a finite lattice and a strongly saturated class $W$. Both premises can hold at every base while the conclusion fails at one base. The same example refutes the assertion with infinity-categorical localizations in place of ordinary localizations.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.12, statement and following argument; sections/E_b062.tex
notes: Six-element lattice counterexample; both ordinary and enhanced localizations; a_b062_verify.py.

statement: Ordinary homotopy categories do not supply coherent gluing. A gluing theorem for the enhanced fine theories cannot in general be replaced by the same pullback or lax-pullback construction on their homotopy categories. The comparison $\Ho\Fun([1],\mathcal V)\to\Fun([1],\Ho\mathcal V)$ need not be faithful, even for $\mathcal V=D(\mathbb Z)$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.13, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Coherent arrow category differs from arrows in the homotopy category; derived integer-coefficient example.

statement: The precise modality and locally cartesian closed comparison. Let $L:\Spaces\to\mathcal V$ be an accessible reflective localization of spaces. The following conditions are equivalent: $L$ is a nullification; its local objects are closed under dependent sums over local bases, hence form a modality; the canonical map \[ L(X\times_Z A)\longrightarrow LX\times_Z A \] is an equivalence for every $X\to Z\leftarrow A$ with $A,Z$ local; and $\mathcal V$ is locally cartesian closed. Consequently these are additional equivalent conditions in E.8. The modality's left class consists of maps with $L$-contractible homotopy fibres and can be strictly smaller than the class inverted by $L$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, E.14, statement and following argument; sections/E.tex
notes: Accessible localizations of spaces; explicit proof of the LCC converse using point diagrams.

statement: The operations supplied by Der 1--4. Let $\D$ be a derivator on all $\mathbb U$-small categories, with presheaf variance, satisfying Der 1--4: coproducts of indexing categories give products, evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms, restriction has both Kan adjoints, and the pointwise comma formulas hold. Then every $f:X\to Y$ has \[ f_!\dashv f^*\dashv f_*:\D(X)\rightleftarrows\D(Y), \] where the display denotes the three functors with their usual alternating directions.
