For $A\in\D(X)$ and $y\in Y$ the formulas are \[ (f_!A)_y\cong\colim_{(y\backslash X)^{\op}} A, \qquad (f_*A)_y\cong\lim_{(X/y)^{\op}} A. \] The diagram under each limit is restriction along the forgetful functor to $X$, interpreted as a coherent diagram in the derivator. Comma squares are homotopy exact. Exact squares are closed under horizontal and vertical pasting, with the direction of their two-cell fixed. Strongness, pointedness and stability are not needed for these statements.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.1, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Der 1–4 and canonical mate pasting; no strongness assumed.

statement: The two strict base-change theorems and their converses. Consider a strict pullback square \[ \begin{tikzcd} X'\ar[r,"g'"]\ar[d,"f'"']&X\ar[d,"f"]\\ Y'\ar[r,"g"']&Y. \end{tikzcd} \] The canonical maps, with source category $\D(X)$ and target category $\D(Y')$, are \[ f'_!g'^*\longrightarrow g^*f_!,\qquad g^*f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^*. \] The first is invertible if $f$ is $W_\infty$-smooth or $g$ is $W_\infty$-proper. The second is invertible if $f$ is $W_\infty$-proper or $g$ is $W_\infty$-smooth. Conversely, $f$ is proper if its right comparison is invertible for every such square with space-valued presheaves and all coefficients; the dual assertion characterizes smoothness by universal left base change.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.2, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Converse tests terminal coefficients on the left adjoint mate, not on the original right comparison.

statement: Unrestricted pullback base change. The left or right Kan half is not a formalism satisfying its corresponding base-change identity for all strict pullback squares of $\Cat$. Failure already occurs for endpoint inclusions into $[1]$, with discrete finite coefficients. It also occurs with stable coefficients.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.3, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Empty endpoint pullbacks; exact finite checks and nonzero stable version.

statement: The projection formula on the smooth half. Let $\D$ be a symmetric monoidal derivator whose external tensor preserves homotopy colimits separately, in the sense of \citet[Definitions 3.23 and 3.25]{EFGPS2014b}. If $f:X\to Y$ is $W_\infty$-smooth, then for $A\in\D(X)$ and $B\in\D(Y)$ the canonical projection map \[ f_!(A\otimes f^*B)\longrightarrow f_!A\otimes B \] is invertible. More generally this map is invertible for an arbitrary $f$ when $B$ is locally constant. The external formula \[ (f\times\id_Z)_!(A\boxtimes C)\cong f_!A\boxtimes C \] holds for every $f$, every small $Z$, and every $C\in\D(Z)$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.4, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Internal formula for smooth maps or locally constant second coefficient; external formula for all maps.

statement: Monoidality alone does not give an internal projection formula for all maps. Even for space-valued or stable presheaves the projection formula of F.4 fails for a general functor. Thus the unqualified monoidality assertion in Lead 3 needs its map or coefficient hypothesis.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.5, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Monoidality alone is insufficient for the internal projection formula; finite endpoint check.

statement: The right projection formula and its precise restrictions. For any functor $f$ and any dualizable object $B$ of the monoidal category $\D(Y)$, the right projection comparison \[ f_*A\otimes B\longrightarrow f_*(A\otimes f^*B) \] is invertible. For proper $f$ it is also invertible whenever tensoring with $B_y$ preserves the homotopy limits indexed by $X_y^{\op}$, for every $y$. In a stable monoidal derivator this includes homotopy-finite fibres, for arbitrary $B$. Without such restrictions the right projection formula is false, even for a proper and smooth projection.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.6, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Global dualizability or pointwise preservation of fibre limits is stated explicitly.

statement: Exchange formulas obtained by taking mates. Suppose $\D$ is closed symmetric monoidal. For every $f:X\to Y$ there is a canonical isomorphism \[ f_*\underline{\Hom}_X(f^*B,A) \cong\underline{\Hom}_Y(B,f_*A). \] For smooth $f$, put $f^!=f^*$ as the right adjoint of $f_!$. The projection formula then gives \begin{align*} f_*\underline{\Hom}_X(A,f^!B)&\cong \underline{\Hom}_Y(f_!A,B),\\ f^!\underline{\Hom}_Y(B,C)&\cong \underline{\Hom}_X(f^*B,f^!C). \end{align*} The right adjoint mate of the left base-change isomorphism in F.2 is \[ f^*g_*\cong g'_*f'^*. \] All these isomorphisms have the coherence inherited from their specified adjunctions.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.7, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Closed exchange and right-adjoint mates; all source and target functors specified.

statement: Why the adjunction directions reverse. Define the opposite derivator by $\D^\vee(S)=\D(S^{\op})^{\op}$. Then \[ f_!^{\D^\vee}=((f^{\op})_*^{\D})^{\op},\qquad f_*^{\D^\vee}=((f^{\op})_!^{\D})^{\op}. \] Opposition of indexing categories exchanges incoming and outgoing lifting categories, hence exchanges smooth and proper maps. The reversal of the adjunction arrows additionally uses opposition of the coefficient categories. Base opposition alone supplies a comparison of the two fine theories over opposite bases; it is not a duality of coefficients over a fixed base. Nor need $\D^\vee$ be monoidal with a separately cocontinuous tensor.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.8, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Both coefficient opposition and base opposition are needed to reverse adjunctions.

statement: Open--closed extensions and stable recollement. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow X$ be a sieve and $i:B\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary cosieve. For a pointed derivator there are adjunctions \[ j^?\dashv j_!\dashv j^*\dashv j_* ,\qquad i_!\dashv i^*\dashv i_*\dashv i^! . \] All four Kan extensions are fully faithful; $j_!$ and $i_*$ are extension by zero. In a stable derivator there are coherent fibre--cofibre sequences \[ j_!j^*A\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow i_*i^*A, \qquad i_*i^!A\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow j_*j^*A. \] Strongness is not needed for these coherent constructions. A triangulated recollement on the ordinary values follows when the stable derivator is strong.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.9, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Coherent sequences without Der5; strongness only for triangulated recollement.

statement: A correspondence formalism on the smooth class, with an enhancement. Let $\mathcal V$ be a $\mathbb V$-presentable closed symmetric monoidal infinity-category whose tensor preserves $\mathbb U$-small colimits separately. Regard the ordinary category $\Cat_{\mathbb U}$ as an infinity-category by its nerve, so its pullbacks are the strict categorical pullbacks. Put $E=\Liss_{W_\infty}$. There is a lax symmetric monoidal functor \[ \Corr(N\Cat_{\mathbb U})_{E,\mathrm{all}} \longrightarrow\Cat_{\infty,\mathbb V},\qquad S\longmapsto\Fun(NS^{\op},\mathcal V), \] sending a span $X\xleftarrow{a}M\xrightarrow{b}Y$, $b\in E$, to $b_!a^*$. It is a pre-six-functor formalism in \citet[Definitions A.5.1 and A.5.6]{EFMann2022} and a six-functor formalism in Definition A.5.7 there. The restriction to homotopy categories is the indicated half of the represented derivator. This assertion uses the given infinity-category, not merely its valuewise homotopy categories.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.10, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Base is nerve of ordinary Cat with strict pullbacks; enhancement and separate cocontinuity explicit.

statement: The terminology of the resulting operations. In F.10 every allowed map has $f^!=f^*$ and $f^!\one=\one$, compatibly with base change. Thus all these maps satisfy the cohomological smoothness formula with the trivial invertible twist; in the usual terminology for this identity they are cohomologically \emph{\'{e}tale}. This does not say that a Grothendieck-proper functor has $f_!=f_*$. Even a functor belonging to both Grothendieck classes need not have this ambidexterity. For a discrete bifibration with finite fibres, however, a stable coefficient category has the canonical ambidexterity $f_!\simeq f_*$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.11, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Kan exceptional inverse image is restriction; Grothendieck properness does not make left and right Kan functors equal.

statement: The all-smooth class does not satisfy the later diagonal convention. The class $E=\Liss_{W_\infty}$ in F.10 is not closed under diagonals. Hence it is not a geometric setup under \citet[Definition 2.1.1 and Remark 2.1.2]{EFHeyerMann2024}, which add this requirement to the earlier convention. Restricting $E$ to discrete fibrations does satisfy the later convention and gives a six-functor formalism by the same construction. In that restriction the preceding cohomological \emph{\'{e}tale} description is unchanged.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.12, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: All-smooth class fails diagonal closure; discrete fibrations give a precise smaller setup.

statement: H\"ormann's diagram correspondences and the enhancement boundary. Fibered multiderivators encode the two halves and their exchange maps on the appropriate 2-multicategory of diagram correspondences. In \citet[Theorem 6.12]{EFHormann2017}, for pre-multiderivators $\mathbb E,\mathbb S$ satisfying Der 1--2, a strict morphism $\mathbb E\to\mathbb S$ is a left, respectively right, fibered multiderivator precisely when the induced map $\mathrm{Dia}^{\mathrm{cor}}(\mathbb E)\to\mathrm{Dia}^{\mathrm{cor}}(\mathbb S)$ is a 1-opfibration, respectively 1-fibration, of 2-multicategories. A closed monoidal derivator supplies the associated diagram-level six-operation structure. This does not turn all strict pullback squares of ordinary categories into exact squares and does not itself construct an infinity-categorical enhancement of an abstract derivator.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.13, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Theorem 6.12 is used with its actual pre-multiderivator hypotheses; no enhancement is manufactured.

statement: Comparison with relative smoothness and properness. For the indexed enhanced category $S\mapsto\Fun(NS^{\op},\Spaces)$ on the ordinary category $\Cat$ with strict pullbacks, the smooth and proper calibrations of \citet[Definition 2.3.1]{EFAnelWeinberger2025} are exactly $\Liss_{W_\infty}$ and $\Prop_{W_\infty}$ in our convention. This is a statement about that indexed category and that base category; replacing its base by $\Cat_\infty$ changes the pullback test.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.14, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Indexed presheaf calibration over the ordinary base Cat, not an unstated Cat-infinity pullback theorem.

statement: The genus-zero category and its geometric coefficients. For $n\geq3$, let $\Gamma_n$ be the pure orientation-preserving mapping class group of the $n$-punctured sphere. Let $\mathcal C_n$ have as objects the isotopy classes of essential multicurves, including the empty multicurve, and put \[ \Hom_{\mathcal C_n}(\sigma,\tau) =\{g\in\Gamma_n:g\sigma\supseteq\tau\}/\Delta_\sigma, \qquad [h]\circ[g]=[hg], \] where $\Delta_\sigma$ is generated by the Dehn twists in the curves of $\sigma$ and acts on the right. Set $T_{0,n}=\mathcal C_n^{\op}$. The exit category of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$ with its dual-tree stratification is $N\mathcal C_n$. For every compactly generated presentable infinity-category $\mathcal V$, \[ \Shv_{\mathrm{cbl}}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C);\mathcal V) \simeq\Fun(N\mathcal C_n,\mathcal V) =\Fun(NT_{0,n}^{\op},\mathcal V). \] Forgetting the last mark induces $Q:\mathcal C_{n+1}\to\mathcal C_n$, $\sigma\mapsto q\sigma$, $[g]\mapsto[\phi(g)]$, and $F=Q^{\op}:T_{0,n+1}\to T_{0,n}$. Here $q$ erases curves which become peripheral and identifies repeated isotopy classes, and $\phi:\Gamma_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma_n$ is the forgetful homomorphism.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.15, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Explicit mapping-class quotient category; stability range and coefficient hypotheses fixed.

statement: Forgetting a mark is proper and need not be smooth. For every $n\geq3$, $F:T_{0,n+1}\to T_{0,n}$ is $W_\infty$-proper. For $n=4$ it is not $W_\infty$-smooth: a specified lifting category is equivalent to $B\mathbb Z$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.16, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Proper for every n>=3; at n=4 an incoming lifting category is BZ, so not smooth.

statement: Geometric direct image and the boundary squares in this example. In the coefficient equivalence of F.15, the categorical right Kan functor $F_*$ is the ordinary topological direct image of constructible sheaves for $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n+1}(\mathbb C)\to\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$. Categorical right base change agrees with topological proper base change for point fibres and for the squares obtained by a closed boundary inclusion. A boundary is represented by the replete full cosieve in the entrance category whose multicurves contain a curve with the specified label partition. The left Kan half supplies no universal smooth base-change statement for this forgetful functor.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.17, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: STRATA geometric direct image and boundary base change
notes: Constructibility checked; fibre exit categories and replete boundary cosieves identify the canonical comparisons.

statement: Indexing an abstract derivator by strict higher categories. For a specified extension of an ordinary derivator to strict $n$-categorical indexing shapes, $2\leq n\leq\omega$, with lax or colax comma objects and a chosen Street-nerve weak-equivalence class, does the corresponding universal smooth/proper lifting condition imply the two base-change isomorphisms of F.2, with coherent mates? We have not established this statement. Even $n=2$ requires an explicit higher Der~4 and an invariance theorem for the chosen lax comma construction; neither is part of an ordinary derivator on $\Cat$. The model-structure claim discussed in Part C supplies neither datum. No proof in Part F uses that unrefereed claim.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.18, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: No proof depends on OpenAI 2026; first undecided case n=2 needs a higher Der4 and mate compatibility.

statement: An exact proper class in the diagonally closed setup. In the discrete-fibration setup of F.12, take $\mathcal V=\Sp$ or $D(k)$ for a nonzero commutative ring $k$. For a discrete fibration $p:E\to S$, the following are equivalent: $p$ is cohomologically proper in \citet[Definition 4.6.1(b)]{EFHeyerMann2024}; after every strict base change its left and right presheaf Kan extensions are naturally equivalent; and $p$ is a discrete bifibration with finite fibres. Finiteness is pointwise and requires no uniform bound. For this class the canonical comparison $p_!\to p_*$ is the finite biproduct equivalence.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, F.19, statement and following argument; sections/F.tex
notes: Exact cohomological properness classification for discrete fibrations with spectra or nonzero commutative-ring coefficients; canonical norm only after checking diagonal properness.

statement: The exact stability input and the available tensor action. In a stable derivator satisfying Der~1--4, homotopy finite limits commute with arbitrary homotopy colimits. Every such derivator has a canonical action by the derivator of spectra. Consequently a right homotopy finite right Kan extension can be expressed as a weighted homotopy colimit with a spectral profunctor as weight. No internal monoidal structure on the coefficient derivator and no strongness axiom are included in this assertion.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.1, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: Der 1-4; no strongness or internal tensor assumed

statement: The canonical dualizing weight and its exact variance. Let $S$ be homotopy finite. Write \[ R_s(t)=\Sigma^\infty_+\operatorname{Hom}_S(t,s),\qquad w_S(s)=\lim_{t\in S^{\mathrm{op}}}R_s(t). \tag{G.2a} \] Then $w_S:S\to\mathrm{Sp}$ is a covariant spectral diagram, with finite-spectrum values, and for every stable derivator there is a canonical natural isomorphism \[ p_*^S F\simeq w_S\otimes_{[S]}F =\int^{s\in S} w_S(s)\otimes F(s). \tag{G.2b} \] The integral denotes the derived coend, with its coherent spectral action. It is not an objectwise tensor followed by the ordinary colimit over $S^{\mathrm{op}}$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.2, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: w_S(s)=lim_t Hom(t s)_+; a derived coend with opposite variance

statement: A pointwise dualizing-object twist already fails on one arrow. The assertion that every homotopy finite $S$ admits $\omega\in\operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Sp})$ with \[ p_*^SF\simeq p_!^S(\omega\otimes F) \quad\hbox{for all }F \tag{G.3} \] where the tensor is pointwise, is false. It remains false for pointwise perfect complexes over a nonzero field.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.3, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: Counterexample [1] with F1 nonzero and F0 zero; also perfect coefficients

statement: Transitivity and base change belong to the kernels. For a functor $u:R\to S$ between homotopy finite categories, set \[ K_u(s,r)=(u_*R_r)(s),\qquad K_u\in\operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}}\times R,\mathrm{Sp}). \] Then $u_*F\simeq K_u\otimes_{[R]}F$. For $v:S\to T$ there are canonical composition and transitivity identities \[ K_{vu}(t,r)\simeq\int^{s\in S}K_v(t,s)\wedge K_u(s,r),\qquad w_R(r)\simeq\int^{s\in S}w_S(s)\wedge K_u(s,r). \tag{G.4} \] A homotopy exact square gives the corresponding base-change equivalence of these kernels and of their weighted functors. No claim that every cartesian square is homotopy exact is needed.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.4, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: Canonical kernel identities; no assertion for arbitrary cartesian squares

statement: The weight is not invariant under unrestricted restriction. The formula $i^*w_S\simeq w_R$ for every functor $i:R\to S$ is false, even for finite posets. Consequently no base-change statement for a ``dualizing object'' may be supplied by ordinary restriction without an additional hypothesis or an extraordinary pullback.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.5, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part G unrestricted dualizing-weight base change
notes: Point selecting 0 of [1] restricts zero whereas point weight is the sphere

statement: A coefficient duality on precisely specified finite objects. For every small $S$, pointwise Spanier--Whitehead duality gives \[ \operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{fin}})^{\mathrm{op}} \simeq\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathrm{Sp}^{\mathrm{fin}}). \tag{G.6a} \] For a ring $A$, derived $A$-linear duality similarly gives \[ \operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Perf}(A))^{\mathrm{op}} \simeq\operatorname{Fun}(S,\operatorname{Perf}(A^{\mathrm{op}})). \tag{G.6b} \] For homotopy finite $S$, all limits and colimits in these formulas remain perfect and $D(p_*^SF)\simeq p_!^{S^{\mathrm{op}}}(DF)$. This is a contravariant duality. In (G.6b) the coefficient ring can be kept unchanged when it is commutative.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.6, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: Contravariant equivalence; opposite ring retained for noncommutative coefficients

statement: Finite EI is not a coefficient-independent extension of homotopy finite. The weighted-colimit assertion for all stable coefficients does not extend from homotopy finite categories to all finite EI categories. For $S=BC_2$ and coefficients $k=\mathbb F_2$, the functor $p_*^S$ does not preserve countable coproducts, and hence cannot be any fixed weighted homotopy colimit on all diagrams.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.7, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: BC2 over F2; homotopy fixed points fail a countable coproduct via sum-to-product map

statement: A finite-group case with its necessary coefficient hypothesis. Let $G$ be a finite group and $k$ a commutative ring in which $|G|$ is invertible. For the derivator of $k$-modules and $S=BG$, the norm gives a natural equivalence $p_!^S\simeq p_*^S$ on all unbounded complexes. In particular this finite EI case has ambidexterity, although G.7 rules out a uniform assertion without the coefficient hypothesis.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.8, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part G coefficient-sensitive finite EI class
notes: All unbounded complexes; no broader EI classification claimed

statement: The exact canonical equivalence criterion for finite posets. For a finite poset $P$ define the colimit-preserving transform \[ (V_PF)(s)= \lim_{t\in P^{\mathrm{op}}} \bigl(\Sigma^\infty_+\operatorname{Hom}_P(t,s)\otimes F(t)\bigr), \qquad V_P:\mathbb D(P)\longrightarrow\mathbb D(P^{\mathrm{op}}). \tag{G.9a} \] There is always a canonical formula \[ p_*^P\simeq p_!^{P^{\mathrm{op}}}V_P. \tag{G.9b} \] For spectra the transform (G.9a) is an equivalence if and only if each strict upper interval $P_{>p}$ is Gorenstein* over $\mathbb Z$. Here a finite poset $L$ is Gorenstein* when every open interval in $L$ with a newly adjoined bottom and top has the integral homology of a sphere; the empty interval is allowed as the $(-1)$-sphere. When this condition holds, (G.9a) gives an equivalence for every stable derivator, and it restricts to pointwise finite spectra or perfect complexes. This is a condition on this canonical transform; it is not a classification of every possible equivalence between the two diagram categories.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.9, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
depends_on: Aoki Theorem A and Proposition 5.12; G.1 G.4
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Lead 4 corrected equivalence; Part G finite posets
notes: Apply Aoki to P opposite; strict upper intervals of P must be Gorenstein-star

statement: Verification of the finite least-vertex geometric dictionary. Let $P$ be a finite poset and $Z=|NP|$. Label a point by the least vertex with positive barycentric coordinate. With downsets open on $P$, this is a continuous map $s:Z\to P$; its strata are contractible, the stratification is conical, and its exit-path infinity-category is $P^{\mathrm{op}}$. Consequently \[ \operatorname{Shv}_{P\text{-}\mathrm{cons}}(Z;\mathcal C) \simeq\operatorname{Fun}(P^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal C) \tag{G.10} \] for spaces, for every compactly assembled coefficient infinity-category, and for every stable presentable coefficient infinity-category. The inverse-image functor from sheaves on the finite downset Alexandrov space $P$ is the fully faithful functor onto the subcategory in (G.10).
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.10, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: STRATA A.4 A.5; Part G prerequisite dictionary
notes: Explicit conical charts and subdivision localization independently checked

statement: Minimum constructibility is not automatically preserved by Verdier duality. Even for $P=[1]$, usual contravariant Verdier duality on $|NP|$ does not preserve the least-vertex constructible sheaves with perfect stalks. Also, the canonical covariant transform $V_P$ in G.9 is not an equivalence for this $P$.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.11, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: Constant sheaf on [0 1]; dualizing stalk zero at boundary and shifted field in interior

statement: A correct geometric Verdier identification with a checked hypothesis. Suppose the finite poset $P$ satisfies the upper-interval criterion of G.9. For $Z=|NP|$ and its minimum map $s:Z\to P$, the spectral transform has the identification \[ V_P\simeq s_+\,\mathbb V_Z\,s^*. \tag{G.12} \] Here $\mathbb V_Z$ is Lurie's covariant sheaf--cosheaf duality and $s_+$ is cosheaf pushforward, with value on $U$ given by the value on $s^{-1}U$. The same identification holds for derived coefficients over a ring. Thus it includes an explicit pushforward of cosheaves; it does not require the ordinary sheaf-valued Verdier dual to stay constructible for the same minimum strata. A concrete class satisfying the criterion is $P=\operatorname{Face}(K)^{\mathrm{op}}$ for any finite simplicial complex $K$, with nonempty faces. In this case the minimum strata on the barycentric subdivision are precisely the open simplices of $K$, so the identification is the usual cellular geometric one.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.12, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: V_P=s_+ V_Z s^*; opposite face posets give actual open-cell strata

statement: The weighted-limit argument does not persist unstably. There is no fixed-colimit-weight description of all finite limits of spaces. Consequently neither the stability argument of G.1 nor its duality conclusions may be exported to unstable fine theories merely because the base is finite.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.13, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: Two discrete objects; product fails binary coproduct preservation

statement: Tilting gives additional equivalences with different data. If $T$ is the path category of a finite oriented tree, then $\mathbb D(T)\simeq\mathbb D(T^{\mathrm{op}})$ for every stable derivator, pseudonaturally in exact morphisms of derivators. More generally any two orientations of the same finite tree are strongly stably equivalent. These are reflection-functor equivalences and are not the assertion that the transform $V_T$ in G.9 is always an equivalence.
where_proved: BISITE_paper.tex, G.14, statement and following argument; sections/G.tex
notes: Reflection functors are additional equivalences and differ from the canonical Frobenius transform
